metadata.title: Another proof of the corona theorem

nodes.name: Maximal ideal space $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)$ and the open unit disc $\Delta$ embedding
nodes.statement: $H^\infty(\Delta)$ is the uniform algebra of bounded analytic functions on $\Delta$; $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)$ its maximal ideal space, into which $\Delta$ embeds via point-evaluation $\phi_z(f)=f(z)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximal ideal space of bounded analytic functions on the disc, with disc embedded by point evaluations.

nodes.name: Fiber $\mathfrak{M}_\alpha$ over $\alpha$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \in \mathbf{T}$, $\mathfrak{M}_\alpha = \{\xi \in \mathfrak{M}(H^\infty) \,;\, \xi(z) = \alpha\}$, where $z$ is the coordinate function.

nodes.name: Cluster set ${\it Cl}(f,\alpha)$
nodes.statement: ${\it Cl}(f,\alpha) = \bigcap_{r>0} \overline{f(\Delta \cap \{|z-\alpha|<r\})}$ for $f \in H^\infty(\Delta)$.

nodes.name: Basic neighborhood $W(\phi, f_1, \dots, f_N, \varepsilon)$
nodes.statement: $W(\phi, f_1,\dots, f_N, \varepsilon) = \{\xi \in \mathfrak{M}(H^\infty) \,;\, |f_k(\xi)-f_k(\phi)| < \varepsilon,\, k=1,\dots,N\}$.

nodes.name: Pseudo-hyperbolic distance $\rho(\eta,\xi)$
nodes.statement: $\rho(\eta,\xi) = \sup\{|f(\eta)| \,;\, f \in H^\infty(\Delta),\, f(\xi)=0,\, \|f\| \le 1\}$, an equivalence relation on $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)$ via $\rho<1$.

nodes.name: Gleason part $P(\xi)$ and analytic disc
nodes.statement: $P(\xi) = \{\eta \in \mathfrak{M}(H^\infty); \rho(\eta,\xi)<1\}$. $P$ is an analytic disc if there is a continuous bijection $L:\Delta \to P$ with $f\circ L$ analytic for all $f \in H^\infty(\Delta)$.

nodes.name: Interpolating sequence and thin (sparse) sequence
nodes.statement: $\{z_j\} \subset \Delta$ is interpolating if for any bounded $\{w_j\}$ there is $f \in H^\infty(\Delta)$ with $f(z_j)=w_j$; equivalently $\inf_k \prod_{j\neq k} |(z_k-z_j)/(1-\overline{z_j}z_k)| > 0$. Thin if this product tends to $1$.

nodes.name: Interpolating Blaschke product
nodes.statement: For an interpolating sequence $\{z_j\}$, $B(z) = \prod_{j=1}^\infty \frac{\overline{z_j}}{|z_j|} \frac{z_j-z}{1-\overline{z_j}z}$.

nodes.name: Hoffman map $L = \lim_\beta L_\beta$
nodes.statement: For $\{c_n\} \subset \Delta$, set $L_n(\zeta) = (\zeta+c_n)/(1+\overline{c_n}\zeta)$. A limit $L$ in $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)^\Delta$ of a convergent subnet $(L_\beta)$ is called a Hoffman map.

nodes.name: Mid-point $c$ of orthogonal arc $C$
nodes.statement: For $-\varepsilon<\alpha<\beta<\varepsilon$, $C$ is the arc from $e^{i\alpha}$ to $e^{i\beta}$ orthogonal to $\mathbf{T}$ inside $\Delta$; the mid-point is $c = C \cap \{t e^{i(\alpha+\beta)/2}\}$.

nodes.name: Sector $S[s,t)$
nodes.statement: $S[s,t) = \{re^{i\theta} \,;\, r \in [s,t),\, |\theta| \le (1-\ell)/2\}$ for $\ell \le s < t \le 1$.

nodes.name: Algebra $(SB)(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$ over $\Delta\times\mathbf{N}^\infty$
nodes.statement: For $h \in B(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$, $g(\zeta,j)= h\circ L_j(\zeta)$ for $j \in \mathbf{N}$ and $g(\zeta,\infty)= H(\zeta)$. $(SB)(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$ is the closed subalgebra of $H^\infty(\Delta\times\mathbf{N}^\infty)$ generated by such $g$.

nodes.name: Cluster value theorem (classical, single function)
nodes.statement: $\textit{Cl}(f,\alpha) = f(\mathfrak{M}_\alpha)$ for all $f \in H^\infty(\Delta)$.

nodes.name: Strong cluster value theorem (Main Theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $B(\mathfrak{F})$ be the uniformly closed subalgebra of $H^\infty(\Delta)$ generated by a countable family $\mathfrak{F}$. If $\phi \in \mathfrak{M}_1$, there is a sequence $\{\zeta_j\} \subset \Delta$ with $\zeta_j \to 1$ and $f(\zeta_j) \to f(\phi)$ for each $f \in B(\mathfrak{F})$.

nodes.name: Corona theorem (Carleson)
nodes.statement: If $f_1,\dots,f_N \in H^\infty(\Delta)$ satisfy $|f_1(z)|+\cdots+|f_N(z)| \ge \delta > 0$ on $\Delta$, then there exist $g_1,\dots,g_N \in H^\infty(\Delta)$ with $\sum_k f_k g_k \equiv 1$.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 — Shilov boundary lies in closure of $\Delta$
nodes.statement: If $f_1,\dots,f_N \in H^\infty(\Delta)$ are constant on the minimal support $S_\phi$ of the representing measure for $\phi$, then $W(\phi,f_1,\dots,f_N,\varepsilon)\cap \Delta \neq \emptyset$ for all $\varepsilon>0$. Hence $X \subset \overline{\Delta}$ in $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)$.
assumptions: $S_\phi$ is the minimal support of the representing measure for $\phi$

nodes.name: Lemma 2.2 — Thin interpolating sequence yields homeomorphic analytic disc
nodes.statement: Let $\{c_n\}$ be a thin interpolating sequence with $c_n \to 1$ and $L$ a Hoffman map by a convergent subnet of $\{L_n\}$. Set $\xi = L(0) \in \mathfrak{M}_1$. Then $P(\xi)$ is an analytic disc in $\mathfrak{M}_1$ and $L:\Delta \to P(\xi)$ is an analytic homeomorphism.
assumptions: $\{c_n\}$ is a thin interpolating sequence in $\Delta$ with $c_n \to 1$
$L = \lim_\beta L_\beta$ is a Hoffman map (convergent subnet of $L_n$)

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 — Closure characterization via thin interpolating sequences
nodes.statement: $\phi \in \mathfrak{M}_1$ lies in $\overline{\Delta}$ iff for every countable $\mathfrak{F} \subset H^\infty(\Delta)$ there is a thin interpolating sequence $\{\zeta_j\}$ with $\zeta_j \to 1$ and $f(\zeta_j) \to f(\phi)$ on $B(\mathfrak{F})$. Moreover such a $\xi \in \mathfrak{M}_1$ with $P(\xi)$ homeomorphic to $\Delta$ exists with $f(\phi)=f(\xi)$ on $B(\mathfrak{F})$.
conclusions: $\phi \in \overline{\Delta}$ iff for every countable $\mathfrak{F}$ a thin interpolating sequence $\{\zeta_j\}$ realizes \eqref{eq1.2} on $B(\mathfrak{F})$
Existence of $\xi \in \mathfrak{M}_1$ with $P(\xi)$ homeomorphic to $\Delta$ and $f(\phi)=f(\xi)$ on $B(\mathfrak{F})$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1 — Simple-function approximation to $\phi(f_k)$
nodes.statement: For $f_1,\dots,f_N \in H^\infty(\Delta)$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a simple function $s(\theta)=\sum_{i=1}^\ell a_i \chi_{E_i}(\theta)$ with support in $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$, $\int s\, dm = 1$, and $|\phi(f_k)-\int_E f_k(\theta)s(\theta)\, dm(\theta)| < \varepsilon$.
conclusions: Existence of $s(\theta)=\sum_i a_i \chi_{E_i}(\theta)$ with $a_i>0$, support in $(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.2 — Extension to algebra generated by $\mathfrak{F}^\sharp$
nodes.statement: (a) Refining $s$ for $\mathfrak{F}^\sharp = \{f_1,\dots,f_N\}\cup\{1,z,B\}$ gives $s^\sharp$ on a subset $F \subset E$ satisfying $|\phi(g) - \int_F g s^\sharp\, dm| < \varepsilon$ for $g \in \mathfrak{F}^\sharp$. (b) A sequence $\{s_j^\sharp\}$ achieves $\phi(g) = \lim_j \int g s_j^\sharp\, dm$ for $g \in B(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$.
assumptions: $\mathfrak{F}^\sharp = \{f_1,\dots,f_N\}\cup\{1,z,B\}$ with a fixed Blaschke product $B$ and the coordinate $z$
conclusions: Existence of $s^\sharp(\theta)$ supported on $F\subset E$ with $\int_F s^\sharp dm=1$ and \eqref{eq3.2} for all $g \in \mathfrak{F}^\sharp$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.3 — Möbius change-of-variables
nodes.statement: $L_c^{-1}$ maps $\overline{\Delta}$ onto itself, $L_c^{-1}(c)=0$, and $L_c^{-1}(e^{i\alpha}) = -L_c^{-1}(e^{i\beta})$. For $g \in L^1(\mathbf{T})$, $\int_{L_c^{-1}(A)} (g\circ L_c)(\theta)\, |L_c'(\theta)|\, dm(\theta) = \int_A g(\theta)\, dm(\theta)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 — Blaschke-product lower bound from small zero sums
nodes.statement: For $0<\eta<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta(\varepsilon,\eta)>0$ such that any Blaschke product $B$ with $\sum_k(1-|z_k|) < \delta$ satisfies $|B(z)| > 1-\varepsilon$ on $|z|\le\eta$.
conclusions: There exists $\delta=\delta(\varepsilon,\eta)>0$ such that $\sum_k (1-|z_k|) < \delta$ implies $|B(z)| > 1-\varepsilon$ on $|z|\le \eta$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2 — $B\circ L_c$ is Blaschke with translated zeros
nodes.statement: If $B$ is Blaschke with $Z(B)=\{z_k\}$, then $B\circ L_c$ is Blaschke with $Z(B\circ L_c) = \{L_c^{-1}(z_k)\}$. For any $\delta>0$ there is $N$ with $\sum_{k\ge N}(1-|L_c^{-1}(z_k)|) < \delta$.
conclusions: For each $\delta>0$ there is $N$ with $\sum_{k\ge N}(1-|L_c^{-1}(z_k)|) < \delta$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.3 — Construction of Blaschke product with $B\circ L_{n_j}\to G$
nodes.statement: For $\phi \in \mathfrak{M}_1$ and a sequence $\{c_n\}\to 1$, there is a Blaschke product $B$ with $B(\phi)=0$ and a subsequence $\{c_{n_j}\}$ with $B(c_{n_j})=0$ such that $B\circ L_{n_j}(\zeta) \to G(\zeta)=\zeta$ uniformly on compacts of $\Delta$.
conclusions: Existence of a Blaschke product $B$ with $B(\phi)=0$
$B\circ L_{n_j}(\zeta)$ converges uniformly on compact subsets of $\Delta$ to $G(\zeta)=\zeta$

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4 — Boundary convergence of $B\circ L_{n_k}$
nodes.statement: Under Lemma 4.3, a subsequence $\{c_{n_k}\}$ exists such that $B\circ L_{n_k}(\theta) \to G(\theta)=e^{i\theta}$ for $m$-a.e. $\theta \in \mathbf{T}$, hence $\widehat{m}$-a.e. on $X$.
conclusions: A subsequence $\{c_{n_k}\}$ such that $B\circ L_{n_k}(\theta) \to G(\theta)=e^{i\theta}$, $m$-a.e. on $\mathbf{T}$

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 — Limit identities for $h\circ L_j$ and polynomial approximation of $H$
nodes.statement: (a) $\lim_j h\circ L_j(B\circ L_j(\zeta)) = H(\zeta) = \lim_j (H\circ B)\circ L_j(\zeta)$ on compacts; $|h\circ L_j - (H\circ B)\circ L_j| \to 0$ on compacts. (b) Polynomials $p_n$ exist with $\|p_n\|_\infty \le \|H\|_\infty$ and $\|p_n - H\|_1 \to 0$.
conclusions: (a) $\lim_j h\circ L_j(B\circ L_j(\zeta)) = H(\zeta) = \lim_j (H\circ B)\circ L_j(\zeta)$, with vanishing difference uniformly on compacts
(b) Existence of polynomials $p_n$ with $\|p_n\|_\infty\le\|H\|_\infty$ and $\|p_n-H\|_1\to 0$, hence $p_n(\zeta)\to H(\zeta)$ on compacts

nodes.name: Newman's theorem (Blaschke product vanishing at $\phi$)
nodes.statement: For any homomorphism $\phi \in \mathfrak{M}(H^\infty) \setminus X$ there exists a Blaschke product $B_0$ with $B_0(\phi)=0$.
conclusions: There exists a Blaschke product $B_0$ with $B_0(\phi)=0$
nodes.origin_citation: Hoffman 1962, Ch. 10; Garnett, Bounded Analytic Functions, Ch. V Thm 2.2

nodes.name: Wermer's embedding theorem
nodes.statement: Each Gleason part of a logmodular algebra such as $H^\infty(\Delta)$ on $X$ is either a single point or an analytic disc; an inner $Z \in H^2(\mu)$ provides a bijective extension $\widehat{Z}: P(\phi)\to\Delta$ with $\widehat{Z}(\phi)=0$.
assumptions: $P(\phi)$ a nontrivial Gleason part with representing measure $\mu$
conclusions: Each Gleason part is a point or analytic disc
Existence of inner $Z\in H^2(\mu)$ with bijective extension $\widehat{Z}:P(\phi)\to\Delta$ and $\widehat{Z}(\phi)=0$
nodes.origin_citation: Wermer (cf. Leibowitz, Lectures on complex function algebras, Ch. 6)

nodes.name: Hoffman's characterization of analytic discs
nodes.statement: A Gleason part $P(\psi)$ in $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)$ is an analytic disc iff its analytic map equals a Hoffman map $L_\psi = \lim_\beta L_\beta$ for a subnet of $\{L_n\}$ associated with an interpolating sequence $\{c_n\}$.
conclusions: $P(\psi)$ is an analytic disc iff its analytic map is a Hoffman map $L_\psi = \lim_\beta L_\beta$ for an interpolating-sequence subnet
nodes.origin_citation: Hoffman 1967 (Bounded analytic functions and Gleason parts)

nodes.name: Cluster value identity \eqref{1.1}
nodes.statement: $\textit{Cl}(f,\alpha) = f(\mathfrak{M}_\alpha)$, $f \in H^\infty(\Delta)$.

nodes.name: Convergence statement \eqref{eq1.2}
nodes.statement: $\zeta_j \to 1$ and $f(\zeta_j) \to f(\phi)$ for each $f \in B(\mathfrak{F})$.

nodes.name: Möbius map $L_n(\zeta)$ \eqref{eq2.2}
nodes.statement: $L_n(\zeta) = (\zeta + c_n)/(1 + \overline{c_n}\zeta)$, $\zeta \in \Delta$.

nodes.name: Halving identity \eqref{eq3.4}
nodes.statement: $\int_{-\pi}^{\alpha} s(\theta)\, dm(\theta) = 1/4 = \int_{\beta}^{\pi} s(\theta)\, dm(\theta)$.

nodes.name: Sign-decomposition cases \eqref{eq3.5}
nodes.statement: Three regimes for $\alpha,\beta$ depending on $\mu(S_\phi \cap U([0,\varepsilon)))$ being in $[0,1/4]$, $(1/4,3/4]$, $(3/4,1]$.

nodes.name: Representation of $h(\phi)$ via $H(0)$ \eqref{eq5.6}
nodes.statement: $h(\phi) = H(0) = \int_{-\pi}^\pi H(\theta)\, dm(\theta)$ for $h \in B(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Use continuity of each $f_k$ on $X$ to choose an open-closed neighborhood $U=U(E)$ of $S_\phi$, then apply Fatou's theorem on the corresponding boundary set $E$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Combine analyticity of $L$ with Schwarz's lemma applied to $B\circ L$ and Wermer's embedding theorem to deduce $L:\Delta \to P(\xi)$ is a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Replace $\mathfrak{F}$ by countable rational-coefficient polynomials in $\mathfrak{F}$ and use that $\mathfrak{M}_1$ is a peak set so neighborhoods $W(\phi,f_1,\dots,f_j,\varepsilon_j)$ intersect $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: Choose disjoint open-closed $U_i$ covering $S_\phi$ on which each $f_k$ varies by less than $\varepsilon/2$, set $a_i=\mu(U_i\cap S_\phi)/m(E_i)$, and bound the integration error by $\varepsilon/2 + \varepsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: Refine the partition of Lemma 3.1 to make $1, z, B$ vary little; products $f^{m_1}\cdots z^m B^n$ inherit small variation up to a constant $C$, and density of the algebra $\mathfrak{F}_0^\sharp$ in $B(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$ extends \eqref{eq3.3}.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Use the elementary inequality $1-|(z_k-z)/(1-\overline{z_k}z)| \le \frac{1+\eta}{1-\eta}(1-|z_k|)$ on $|z|\le \eta$ and the bound $-\log t \le C(1-t)$ to estimate $\log|B(z)|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: Show $\zeta_k = (z_k-c)/(1-\bar{c}z_k)$ is a Blaschke sequence, and rule out singular factor in the inner function $B\circ L_c$ by composition with $L_c^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: Build sectors $S[s_j,r_j)$ with $r_j=(2s_j+1)/3$, choose $c_{n_j}$ so contributions of zeros in $S[\ell,r_j)\cup S[s_{j+1},1)$ are $<\delta_j/2$; split $B_0=B_1B_2B_3$ and compose with a thin Blaschke product $B_4$ whose zeros yield $B_4\circ L_{n_{2j+1}}\to G$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Compute Taylor coefficients $a_k^{(j)}$ of $B\circ L_{n_j}$, use Lemma 4.3 to show $a_1^{(j)}\to G'(0)=1$, deduce $\|B\circ L_{n_j}-G\|_2\to 0$, then take an a.e.-convergent subsequence.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: (a) Triangle inequality and convergence of $B\circ L_j$ to $G$. (b) Cesàro means $p_n$ of the Fourier series of the bounded function $H$ converge to $H$ in $L^1$ with $\|p_n\|_\infty\le\|H\|_\infty$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (strong cluster value theorem)
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma 3.1, Lemma 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Lemma 4.3, Lemma 4.4 and Lemma 5.1 to show $h(\phi) = H(0) = \lim_j h(\zeta_j)$ for $\zeta_j = c_j$, then invoke Lemma 2.3 to extend from finite $f_1,\dots,f_N$ to a countable family $\mathfrak{F}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary (corona theorem from main theorem)
nodes.statement: Since $W(\phi,f_1,\dots,f_N,\varepsilon)\cap\Delta\neq\emptyset$ by the main Theorem, $\Delta$ is dense in $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)$. Reformulating density via the Bezout-type identity yields the corona conclusion.

nodes.name: Remark — Jensen-measure consequence of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Since $H^\infty(\Delta)$ is logmodular on $X$, $\mu$ is a Jensen measure: if $f_k$ vanishes/constant on a Borel $K$ with $\mu(K)>0$, then $f(\phi)=0$ (resp. $f_k(\phi)=c_k$); however outside analytic discs the integral may diverge.

nodes.name: Remark — Sparse $\{\zeta_j\}$ and analytic discs
nodes.statement: The homomorphism $\phi$ need not lie in the closure of $\{\zeta_j\}$ in $\mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)$; sparse choice of $\{\zeta_j\}$ relates the construction to interpolating sequences and analytic discs.

nodes.name: Remark (a) — Closure of analytic discs
nodes.statement: Each nontrivial analytic disc $P(\phi) \subset \mathfrak{M}(H^\infty)\setminus\Delta$ lies in $\overline{\Delta}$; using Wermer's $Z$, approximations $q_i \to Z$ in $L^2(\mu)$ and Hoffman maps yield interpolating $\{c_j\}$ with $f(c_j)\to f(\phi)$ for $f \in \mathfrak{F}$.

nodes.name: Remark (b) — Continuous-flow representation of $\mathfrak{M}_1$
nodes.statement: Via $H^\infty(\mathbf{R}_+^2) \cong H^\infty(\Delta)$, the fiber $\mathfrak{M}_1$ is partly modeled by the Stone-Čech flow $(\mathbf{X},\{S_t\})$; orbits $\textit{O}(\mathbf{x})\times(0,\infty)$ correspond to analytic discs and minimal sets to non-homeomorphic discs.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\phi \in \mathfrak{M}_1\setminus X$
nodes.statement: By Lemma 2.1 the Shilov boundary $X$ lies in $\overline{\Delta}$, so it suffices to prove the convergence for $\phi$ in the fiber $\mathfrak{M}_1$ minus $X$, where the representing measure $\mu$ is continuous and $S_\phi$ is compact in $\mathfrak{M}_1\cap X$.

nodes.name: Build approximating simple functions $s_n(\theta)$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 3.1 to obtain simple functions $s_n(\theta)=\sum_i a_i^{(n)}\chi_{E_i^{(n)}}$ supported in $(-\varepsilon_n,\varepsilon_n)$ with $\phi(f_k) = \lim_n \int f_k s_n\, dm$.

nodes.name: Choose mid-points $c_n$ of orthogonal arcs
nodes.statement: Pick $\alpha_n,\beta_n$ as in \eqref{eq3.4}–\eqref{eq3.5} and let $c_n = t_n e^{i(\alpha_n+\beta_n)/2} \in \Delta$ be the mid-point of the arc $C_n$ from $e^{i\alpha_n}$ to $e^{i\beta_n}$ orthogonal to $\mathbf{T}$. Then $c_n \to 1$.

nodes.name: Extract thin interpolating subsequence and apply Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: Pass to a thin interpolating subsequence $\{c_{n_j}\}$ for which Lemma 4.3 yields a Blaschke product $B$ with $B(\phi)=0$ and $B\circ L_{n_j}(\zeta) \to G(\zeta)=\zeta$ uniformly on compacts.

nodes.name: Form algebra $B(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$ and limit functions $H$
nodes.statement: Set $\mathfrak{F}^\sharp = \{f_1,\dots,f_N\}\cup\{1,z,B\}$. By a normal-families argument, $h\circ L_j(\zeta) \to H(\zeta)$ uniformly on compacts for each $h \in B(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$ (\eqref{eq5.1}).

nodes.name: Refine simple functions to $s^\sharp_j$ and obtain representing limits
nodes.statement: Lemma 3.2 supplies $\{s^\sharp_j(\theta)\}$ with $\phi(g) = \lim_j \int g s^\sharp_j\, dm$ on $B(\mathfrak{F}^\sharp)$, and combining with Lemma 3.3 gives $\phi(h) = \lim_j \int h\circ L_j(\theta)\, u_j(\theta)\, dm(\theta)$ where $u_j = s^\sharp_j\circ L_j |L_j'|$.

nodes.name: Prove $h(\phi) = H(0)$ via polynomial approximation
nodes.statement: Using $B(\phi)=0=G(0)$, polynomials $p_n$ in $B$ satisfy $p_n\circ B(\phi) = p_n(0)$. By Lemma 5.1(b), $p_n(0) \to H(0)$, so $|h(\phi) - H(0)| \to 0$, giving \eqref{eq5.6}.

nodes.name: Identify $\zeta_j = c_j$ and conclude $h(\phi) = \lim_j h(\zeta_j)$
nodes.statement: Set $\zeta_j = L_j(0) = c_j$. From Lemma 5.1(a), $H(\zeta) = \lim_j h\circ L_j(B\circ L_j(\zeta))$; at $\zeta=0$ and using $B\circ L_j(0)=0$, $h(\phi) = H(0) = \lim_j h\circ L_j(0) = \lim_j h(\zeta_j)$. Hence $f_k(\zeta_j) \to f_k(\phi)$.

nodes.name: Lift from finite $\{f_1,\dots,f_N\}$ to countable $\mathfrak{F}$ via Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Lemma 2.3 then transfers the conclusion from finite families to the uniform algebra $B(\mathfrak{F})$ generated by a countable $\mathfrak{F}\subset H^\infty(\Delta)$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: Initialize sectors and apply Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Set $s_1=\ell$, $r_1=(2s_1+1)/3$, and use Lemma 4.1 to choose $\delta_1$ such that the bound \eqref{eq4.1} holds for $\varepsilon_1,\eta_1$.

nodes.name: Inductive sector selection
nodes.statement: Pick $c_{n_j}$ and $s_j,r_j$ inductively so $\sum_{S[\ell,r_j)\cup S[s_{j+1},1)\cap Z(B_0)}(1-|L_{n_j}^{-1}(z_k)|) < \delta_j/2$, defining sub-Blaschke products $B^{(j)}$ with $|B^{(j)}\circ L_{n_j}(\zeta)|>1-\varepsilon_j$ on $|\zeta|\le \eta_j$.

nodes.name: Split $B_0 = B_1 B_2 B_3$ via parity of sectors
nodes.statement: Define $B_1, B_2, B_3$ by partitioning $Z(B_0)$ by sector parity. Since $B_0(\phi)=0$, either $B_1 B_2$ or $B_1 B_3$ vanishes at $\phi$; assume $(B_1 B_2)(\phi)=0$.

nodes.name: Combine with thin Blaschke product $B_4$
nodes.statement: Replace $\{c_{2j}\}$ by a subsequence so $(B_1 B_2)\circ L_{n_{2j}}(\zeta) \to 1$, choose thin $B_4$ with $B_4\circ L_{n_{2j+1}}(\zeta) \to G(\zeta)$, and set $B = B_1 B_2 B_4$.
